pick.headline: US bombs Baghdad's Amiriyah shelter
pick.summary: On February 13, 1991, two US laser-guided bombs struck the Amiriyah air-raid shelter in Baghdad, killing hundreds of civilians.
pick.significance: Washington said the bunker was a military command center. The deaths caused international outrage and led to tighter controls on targets in Baghdad.
pick.fbis: The East Asia Daily Report of February 14, 1991, carried Hong Kong AFP from Jakarta: Indonesian Foreign Minister Alatas said the U.S. raid on a Baghdad shelter showed war "always" claims innocent victims, as Iraq reported 94 bodies recovered and allied commanders called it a command center.

alternates.headline: Chernenko named Soviet leader
alternates.summary: On February 13, 1984, a Central Committee plenum elected Konstantin Chernenko general secretary of the CPSU, succeeding Andropov.
alternates.significance: The ailing 72-year-old's selection reflected the old guard's reluctance to hand power to a younger generation. He lived only another thirteen months.
alternates.fbis: The Soviet Union Daily Report of February 13, 1984, listed Andropov's mourning and world condolences, then "Konstantin Chernenko Elected General Secretary" with the February 13 plenum, Chernenko's speech on "Ensuring Continuity", Tikhonov's nomination and a TASS biography.

alternates.headline: Two-plus-Four formula on Germany agreed in Ottawa
alternates.summary: On February 13, 1990, the foreign ministers of the two German states and the four wartime Allies agreed in Ottawa to hold 'Two plus Four' talks on the external aspects of German unity.
alternates.significance: The format led to the treaty of September 1990 that restored full German sovereignty.
alternates.fbis: The East Europe Daily Report of February 15, 1990, carried Czechoslovak Foreign Minister Dienstbier, interviewed at Ottawa, explaining that a "two plus four" system had been agreed for German unification, alongside the new ceiling on Soviet and U.S. troops in Europe.
